title: Tenant reshuffle and held-requests rescue plan for partial us-west region degradation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a partial degradation in us-west (infra/network fabric packet loss affecting a subset of GPU hosts) several long-lived requests were held in the edge/proxy layer for tenants pinned to us-west Dedicated pools. This ticket defines a controlled tenant reshuffle (move affected tenant traffic to healthy regions or dedicated fallback pools), a safe rescue plan for held/queued requests, and a short-term kernel-level KV cache re-warm approach to avoid large QoS regression after failover. The goal is to: (1) restore throughput with minimal client errors, (2) preserve request ordering for streaming sessions where possible, and (3) avoid cache stampedes on target region hosts.
runbook_steps: 1) Incident triage: confirm region scope via infra metrics (packet loss, host churn) and trace IDs in request hub; open incident channel #ops-incident-us-west and notify on-call SRE.

2) Identify impacted tenants: query tenant routing table for us-west pinned pools and filter active sessions with 'edge-held' flag in request logs (query: https://dash.redundant/queries/held-requests-us-west).

3) Evaluate fallback availability: check capacity in us-east and eu-west dedicated pools; if dedicated capacity insufficient, evaluate hosted-compatible model variants for temporary routing (model size/latency trade-offs).

4) Controlled traffic shift: update routing policy for affected tenant slice to 'reshuffle-safepath' (gradual 10%, 30%, 60%, 100% steps at 30s intervals) with rapid rollback toggle. Use routing tool: /ops/traffic-shaper --plan reshuffle-safepath --tenants <list>.

5) Held-request rescue: for requests listed as 'held' in proxy queue, perform per-tenant decision: (a) small-duration streaming sessions (<15s) — replay to new region preserving session metadata; (b) long/interactive sessions — send graceful 'retry-in-new-region' websocket frame to client (if supported) and mark session as migrated; (c) stateless requests — replay asynchronously via worker with idempotency keys. Record all replays in replay-log with origin trace IDs.

6) KV cache warm-up: after traffic arrives in target region, prime KV caches using sampled recent prefix tokens from replayed sessions and a short synthetic workload (safe rate-limited tokens per second) to avoid token-latency spike. Recommended: max 100 token/sec per host for first 2 minutes.

7) Monitoring and SLO gates: track request error rate, 95th percentile latency, and token cost delta per tenant. If error rate > 3x baseline or latency > 2x baseline after any reshuffle step, abort and rollback per rollback plan.

8) Post-action verification: ensure KV consistency, confirm no duplicated final outputs (idempotency checks), and update customer-facing incident notes with timestamps of migration and expected >95% throughput restoration.
9) Postmortem tasks: collect shard-level traces, a list of replayed requests, and compute cost delta; schedule a retrospective with support and customer success for affected tenants.

10) Follow-up engineering fixes: implement better proxy backpressure (limit held-requests per tenant), add sticky-session hints for replay, and extend routing policy to incorporate KV cache weight when deciding target hosts.
rollback_steps: a) Immediate rollback trigger conditions: sustained error rate spike >3x or client-reported corruption/dupe outputs; operator can toggle 'reshuffle-safepath' rollback in routing console.

b) Rollback action: revert routing changes to original us-west pinning, drain new-region traffic using connection-cutoff strategy (no new sessions to new region; allow existing to finish) and replay any partially processed held requests back to original hosts when host health returns.
c) KV cleanup: invalidate warmed synthetic prefixes to avoid contaminating cache stats; mark hosts for a controlled cache rebuild once stable.
d) Customer mitigation: if rollback causes degraded experience, engage SRE+CS to open temporary credits and a targeted postmortem timeline.
e) Post-rollback verification: confirm routing table equality with pre-incident state and reconcile billing/telemetry windows for affected tenants.
safety_considerations: Preserve idempotency: all replayed requests must carry original idempotency keys; workers should dedupe outputs before emitting to clients.
Data locality and compliance: for Private/VPC customers with region constraints, respect geo-fencing — only allow reshuffle if tenant has permitted fallback regions listed in tenant metadata.
Authentication continuity: ensure token exchange flow for migrated websocket sessions does not drop auth context; use short-lived session handoff tokens issued by control-plane for migration.
Resource contention: avoid priming KV caches at too high a rate to prevent eviction storms on existing workloads.
Operator safety: all destructive routing changes require two approvers for Dedicated customers with SLA >= Platinum.
